keyFindings.description: B3. TmuxRuntime.stop reports a clean stop when list-panes itself fails: tmux.panePid returns undefined on ANY nonzero exit (tmux.ts:182) -> verifyPaneProcess 'pane-gone' -> stop returns normally -> caller clears the locator. At the merge base stop never consulted list-panes and threw ProcessStopFailed for any kill-pane failure not matching PANE_GONE_STDERR (the invariant the doc still states). A tmux client killed by defaultRunner's 30 s timeout (state/fetch.ts:55-61, nonzero exit, empty stderr) or any transient listing failure with the pane alive now yields: closeTree -> tree closed with a live root untracked; worker retire -> live worker's locator cleared; removeTreeProcess -> second root resumed beside a live one. Reproduced (throwaway TmuxRuntime test: list-panes {exitCode:1, stderr:''} -> stop resolves, commands ['list-panes'] only, nothing thrown). Fix: distinguish 'pane absent' (exit 0 + row missing, or stderr matching PANE_GONE_STDERR) from 'listing failed' in panePid/verifyPaneProcess; stop throws ProcessStopFailed for the latter; probe's pre-existing collapse to dead may stay or become unknown (document). Regression test required.

B4 (narrow). The `missing a pane id` throw sits above the refuseKill return and the verify gate. probe returns not-recorded-process for a pane-id-less locator without touching tmux, but the stop that verdict drives throws; in closeTreeLocked that is anyFailed -> StopFailed -> tree lingering forever, retried every sweep. Pre-PR the probe backfill repaired a live one. Schema-valid input (tmuxPaneId optional on tree/controller locators); deployed state has zero such records, so unreachable on this upgrade, but a self-contradiction with the stop doc. Fix: move refuseKill + verify above the throw (no-identity returns normally, refusal logged) or delete the throw; reconcile the two doc sentences. Reproduced (probe -> not-recorded-process; stop(paneless,100,{refuseKill:true}) throws; zero tmux commands).

refuseKillJudgment: Keep. It is the deciding layer's verdict handed down so the runtime neither re-decides nor re-logs (log-once), and on tmux it cannot skip a kill the runtime's own gate would allow: a pane's root pid and start ticks are launch-fixed, so a not-recorded-process verdict on an identity-bearing locator cannot revert to 'recorded process alive' between probe and stop; every caller sets it from a same-locator probe taken immediately before, and stopProcess's cached-client branch preserves it. Redundant for tmux SAFETY (TmuxRuntime.stop self-gates when the flag is absent) and that is the right shape: no runtime may read the flag's absence as 'kill unconditionally' (neither TmuxRuntime nor FakeRuntime does). The interface doc states the trust relationship plainly. No change requested.
